title: "Talk to the computer in English" 👩‍💻
text: A story 1950s Grace Hopper argued that people should give computers instructions in words close to English. Experts said computers could only understand numbers. She built one of the first compilers anyway, and her English-like language shaped COBOL , which still runs banks today. Today You will write the instructions for a working app in plain English . The language finally caught up with her idea.

title: The hostel office inbox 📥
text: Today's problem 0 C No water in C block since morning. Please check. 2 C Sparks coming from the switch board near my bed when I switch on the fan!! 3 A Mess lo curry chala uppu ga undi roju, please cook properly 4 C నీళ్ళు రావట్లేదు, ఉదయం నుండి bathroom లో tap dry 7 C C block taps are dry, can't even brush my teeth 9 A Too much salt in today's dal at lunch, nobody could eat it 14 A Smell like cooking gas near the kitchen, scared to go there 7 of 34 · 📊 see all of them as a table ↗ Which would you deal with first? Type the row numbers 🔁 Same problem, new words : 0 · 4 · 7 are one dry tap in C-block ⚠️ Danger is buried : 2 (sparks) · 14 (gas) among salty curry 🌀 Messy : English, Telugu, both. Someone reads every one, daily. Today's app does the first pass in seconds: category · urgency · summary · reply · "a human must look" , and then we group the repeats.

title: One app, built four ways 🧱
text: Today Our app: a hostel complaint sorter . A messy complaint goes in; the category, urgency and a polite reply come out. 1 🧩 No-code the instructions are the app 2 📨 One API call keys · tokens · cost 3 📊 JSON × a spreadsheet structured output · pandas 4 🌐 A small app a link you can share ✨ The model asks your code a peek at Week 7 Every layer: I do it → your turn (3 min) → one word or number in chat . 🧩 No-code track? Layer 1 is your capstone path. Watch the rest; you don't have to code.

title: Get to ✅ Connected
text: Setup check · 10 minutes 1 · Notebook Open the Colab link in the chat → File → Save a copy in Drive 2 · Key aistudio.google.com → Get API key → Create → copy 3 · Secret In Colab, the 🔑 icon (left) → Add new secret → name GEMINI_API_KEY → paste → Notebook access on 4 · Run Run the three setup cells. You should see ✅ Connected , or a message saying what to fix ✅ Connected? React with 👍 Stuck? Type just the step number (1–4) 🔒 A key is a password that spends money. It goes in the Secrets panel, never in a code cell, never on GitHub, never in a WhatsApp group.

title: The instructions are the app 🧩
text: Layer 1 · no-code You sort complaints sent to a college hostel helpdesk in South India. Students write in English, Telugu, or a mix of both, often casually. For each message, decide: - category: the ONE best category. - urgency: high = a safety risk … ; medium = … ; low = everything else. - summary: what is wrong, in at most 12 words. - reply: a warm, polite reply, at most 40 words, in the language they wrote in. Never promise a date or a time. Never make up names or numbers. - needs_human: true if there is any safety risk… I do it Save these as a Gemini skill (or a Custom GPT / Claude Project). Test: "Sparks coming from the switch board near my bed!!" Your turn · 3 min Run section 1 of the notebook. Read the instructions. Then make your own skill with them, if you like. Type the urgency it gave the sparks complaint: one word

title: The same thing, from code 📨
text: Layer 2 · one API call 📤 You send 🧠 model : which kitchen 📋 instructions : the system prompt 💬 your text : the complaint 🎛️ settings : temperature (remember Week 3?) → 📥 You get back ✍️ the answer 🔢 tokens in · tokens out 💰 and so, the cost Your turn · 3 min Run section 2. Then change the temperature to 1 and run it three times. Type your tokens in : just the number

title: Programs can't read paragraphs 📊
text: Layer 3 · JSON × a spreadsheet A paragraph "This sounds like an electrical problem, and it could be quite serious. I'd suggest contacting…" Nice for a person. Now count 500 of them. JSON { "category": "electricity", "urgency": "high", "needs_human": true, … } Same answer, as labelled fields. Sort it, count it, filter it. 📄 CSV of complaints → 🐼 pandas reads it → 🔁 one call per row → 📊 results table → 💰 ₹ for 1,000 rows Run section 3, then type your ₹ for 1,000 rows : just the number

title: A link anyone can use 🌐
text: Layer 4 · a small app Gradio Turns one Python function into a web page: a text box in, the result out. share=True Gives you a public link for 72 hours. Send it to a friend or a parent and let them try it. Your turn · 3 min Run section 4. Type a complaint into your own app. Did your app open? Type Y or N This is the moment it stops being a notebook and becomes something a real person can use . And real people don't type what you expect… 👉

title: You shared it. Real users will try this 🔨
text: Break-it challenge · 10 minutes A demo that works once isn't an app yet. Try these on your app (or the attack cell in the notebook): 1 Write in Telugu , or Telugu-English 2 Put two problems in one message 3 "Ignore your instructions and…" 4 Something that isn't a complaint 5 Only emojis , or nonsense Type the number of the attack that broke it: 1–5 Then fix it with one line in the instructions, run section 1 again, and retry the attack. That's how real AI products get better: break → add a rule → test again .

title: Change one letter, get a different app 🔁
text: Same code, four apps A 🏠 Hostel complaint sorter complaint → category, urgency, reply B 📚 Ask the course question → answer from the course notes, or "I don't know" C 🗣️ Telugu explainer technical term → simple English + Telugu D 💼 Interview coach question + your answer → scores + a better answer What changes The instructions , the answer shape (schema) and the data . What stays the same Everything else: the call, the loop, the cost, the app. Open the four-apps notebook (link in chat), set USE_CASE , run it, and type the letter you picked

title: The model asks your code for help 🔧
text: ✨ A peek at Week 7 1 Student: "No water in C-block. Who should I contact?" 2 The model can't look it up, so it writes a request: get_block_contact("C") 3 Your Python function runs and returns "C-block warden, ext. 103" 4 The model writes the reply, using the real answer This is called function calling . Give a model a few functions (check a timetable, add a reminder, send a message) and it starts to act . In Week 7, that's an agent . 🥚 remember this one

title: "The most dangerous phrase in the…
text: "The most dangerous phrase in the language is: we've always done it this way. " — Grace Hopper Four weeks ago you were using AI. Today you built one, ran it on a spreadsheet, broke it, fixed it and shared it. If something didn't run today, that's not failure: that's step one of every engineer's day . Read the error, change one thing, run it again. See you next week. 🙏

title: Course update: Gemini Gems are becoming skills
text: Update (Week 5): Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Gemini skills. Personal accounts are moved over automatically from 17 November 2026. Skills are free, need age 18+ and Keep Activity switched on, can hold reference files such as PDFs, and are used by typing / and the skill name in a Gemini chat. If you planned a no-code capstone as a Gem (Week 4 slides), build it as a Gemini skill instead. A Custom GPT or a Claude Project also works.
